newsitem.title: FRANCE: French dairy industry squeezed in south by strike.
newsitem.headline: French dairy industry squeezed in south by strike.

text.p: Dairy cooperatives have stopped collecting milk from southern French producers because of a shortage of storage space and fuel on the eleventh day of a truckers' strike, the dairy association Atla said on Thursday.
"Collection of milk stopped in the southeast and southwest at midday," an Atla spokeswoman told Reuters.
She said Nestle's Chambourcy plant in Lisieux was affected, and Danone's installations in Paris-Sud and Lesquin were blocked off.
Danone said it had not introduced short-time working, but many other smaller fresh products companies have.
Around 10 percent of France's milk is produced in the south by 20,000 dairy farmers, the Atla spokeswoman said.
The situation in western France is "less catastrophic" because the roadblocks in that region were erected later and many cooperatives had stocked petrol, she said.
